rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Bohr's model (1913)** keeps Rutherford's nucleus but quantises the electron: stationary non-radiating orbits exist only where mvr = nh/2π; light is emitted or absorbed only in jumps (hν = |E₂ − E₁|); Coulomb force supplies the centripetal force.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - mvr = nh/2π (quantisation) - hν = |E₂ − E₁| (frequency condition) - rₙ = 0.529 n²/Z Å; vₙ = 2.18 × 10⁶ Z/n m s⁻¹ - Eₙ = −13.6 Z²/n² eV = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ Z²/n² J - ν̄ = RZ²(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Orbit vs orbital:** orbit = Bohr's fixed circular path; orbital = quantum probability region — different models, different words.  ·  **Emission vs absorption:** falling jump emits hν; rising jump absorbs hν — the frequency condition covers both.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The electron does not radiate energy while it remains in a stationary orbit."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Bohr radius 0.529 Å*** — the ground-state orbit of hydrogen: the ruler of the atomic world.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: postulates of bohr's atomic model, its application (within Atomic Structure).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Quantisation Saves the Atom In 1913 Niels Bohr repaired Rutherford's model by adding one idea: the electron's angular momentum is **quantised**. Only certain orbits exist, no radiation is emitted inside them, and light appears only when the electron jumps between orbits. The model works exactly for hydrogen and one-electron ions (He⁺, Li²⁺).  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The postulates (state in order — NEB 3m) 1. **Stationary orbits:** the electron revolves only in certain permitted circular orbits (stationary states) of fixed energy and does **not** radiate while in one. 2. **Quantisation of angular momentum:** only orbits satisfying mvr = nh/2π (n = 1, 2, 3, …) are allowed. 3.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "r ∝ n²/Z; v ∝ Z/n; E ∝ −Z²/n² — remember which quantity squares what."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (3m): Using Eₙ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸/n² J, calculate the energy of the electron in the second orbit of hydrogen.** — E₂ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸/(2)² = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸/4 = **−5.45 × 10⁻¹⁹ J**. The negative sign shows the electron is bound; the zero of energy is at infinite separation.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For hydrogen-like ions multiply by Z² (energy) or divide by Z (radius) — He⁺ questions are the standard variant.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Angular-momentum quantisation** — the single postulate that creates discrete energy levels and hence line spectra.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Postulates: stationary non-radiating orbits; mvr = nh/2π; hν = |E₂ − E₁|; Coulomb = centripetal. Results: rₙ = 0.529 n²/Z Å; Eₙ = −13.6 Z²/n² eV. NEB 2022: E₂ = −5.45 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bor's model earned the 1922 Nobel Prize and still anchors every energy-level diagram in spectroscopy.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Bohr's model was proposed in: → C  ·  Angular momentum quantisation is: → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### Deep dive — Bohr's four rules and what each one buys Bohr (1913) rescued the Rutherford atom with two quantisation rules and two classical ones: 1. **Stationary states** — the electron moves only in certain circular orbits (mvr = nh/2π), and while in one it does *not* radiate, although classical physics demands that an accelerating charge must.…  ·  **Bohr's postulates → what each explains** | Postulate | Statement | Explains | |---|---|---| | Stationary states | Electron radiates nothing while in an allowed orbit | Why atoms are stable at all | | Quantised angular momentum | mvr = nh/2π | Why only certain orbits exist | | Jump condition | hν = E₂ − E₁ | Line spectra and the Rydberg formula | |…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Rutherford (Topic 13):** Bohr keeps the nucleus and quantises the orbits. - **To hydrogen spectrum (Topic 15):** the frequency condition generates every spectral series. - **To de Broglie (Topic 17):** the wave view explains *why* mvr = nh/2π — n wavelengths must fit the orbit's circumference.
